findings.where: electron/lib/autonomyGate.cjs — stripSpellings()/normalisePath()/namesGovernedPath(), consumed by inspectCreate at BOTH origins and by upgradeApplier.applyWith step 3; electron/lib/upgradeApplier.cjs — spellingRefusal()/validatePath(), which canonicalise characters but never ask the filesystem what file a path names; scripts/verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs §13 variants(), whose ten spellings do not include a short basename
findings.problem: An NTFS 8.3 SHORT BASENAME is a fourth synonym the fence does not canonicalise, and the governed bytes do not survive it. 8.3 generation is live on this volume for the real worktree, not only a scratch fixture: dir /x in electron/lib lists AUTONO~1.CJS autonomyStop.cjs, AUTONO~2.CJS autonomyPolicy.cjs, AUTONO~3.CJS autonomyGate.cjs, LOYALT~1.CJS loyaltyGuard.cjs, and in shared/ LOYALT~1.JSO loyalty-tripwire.json. Measured end to end on this platform in a scratch repository root with the REAL policy, capability and loyaltyGuard modules, master-approved, action 'patch', baseSha256 read through the spelling: gate.namesGovernedPath('electron/lib/AUTONO~1.CJS') returns null; applier.spellingRefusal returns null; readFileSync through the spelling returns the real file's bytes so the baseSha256 base-drift check PASSES rather than catching it; loyaltyGuard.inspectChanges refuses nothing, with or without the new gate.normalisePath canonicalisation; and the apply APPLIED, leaving electron/lib/autonomyStop.cjs reading "function isStopped(){return false;}". Identical results and identical byte clobbering for electron/lib/autonomyPolicy.cjs via AUTONO~2.CJS, the PROTECTED electron/lib/loyaltyGuard.cjs via LOYALT~1.CJS, and shared/loyalty-tripwire.json (the tamper-evidence baseline) via LOYALT~1.JSO. This is the FOURTH spelling class in four review rounds that this fence has failed to canonicalise (round 1: unresolved structure; round 2: trailing dot and space, graded NIT because the bytes survived; round 3: the ::$DATA stream suffix) and the SECOND whose governed bytes do not survive. It differs from the previous three in kind, not just in detail: AUTONO~1.CJS shares a six-character prefix with the long name and nothing else, so no transform over the characters can recover the governed name, and a fifth filesystem synonym would defeat the same way. It is ALSO worse than round 3 in reach. At origin 'ipc' the long name electron/lib/autonomyStop.cjs IS refused by the new fence for every kind — that fence works — but the short name is ALLOWED (measured: ipc=ALLOWED, rama=refused, where the rama refusal is only the stop firing on a default install and evaporates the moment master writes an allow-file). So the renderer route is live rather than latent: a tier-1 proposals:create with kind 'self-modify' and path 'electron/lib/AUTONO~1.CJS' passes the new fence, and electron/ipc/timeline.cjs's pre-existing SELF_MODIFY applier at lines 204-205 does fs.writeFileSync(change.path, change.content, 'utf8') with no root confinement. Bounds, so the severity is not overstated: I6 and I17 are INTACT — every write required master's recorded approval, proposals.apply has no in-process caller, fileProposal has no caller at all, and no autonomy rung was climbed; the timeline.cjs write primitive is PRE-EXISTING and named as an unclosed residual in autonomyGate's own header. What is new is that this slice's fence refuses the long name and waves the short one through, and that master reviewing a diff containing AUTONO~1.CJS is shown a name that does not say what it addresses. In-scope item 1, "the STOP unreachable by any proposal", is therefore still false.
findings.fix: Change the method rather than adding a fifth transform. Measured on this platform: fs.realpathSync('…/AUTONO~1.CJS') returns the short path unchanged and is useless here, but fs.realpathSync.native('…/AUTONO~1.CJS') returns '…/electron/lib/autonomyStop.cjs' AND fs.realpathSync.native('…/autonomyStop.cjs::$DATA') returns the same canonical long path — it asks the filesystem instead of the characters, so it closes all four spellings at once and any fifth that is a filesystem synonym. (1) In upgradeApplier.validatePath, after the existing resolve-and-confine step, canonicalise the resolved target with fs.realpathSync.native and carry that canonical path on the returned target; for a 'create' the target does not exist yet and native throws, so canonicalise the NEAREST EXISTING ANCESTOR and append the remainder — the same walk writabilityOf already does. Refuse plainly, naming the path, if the canonical form cannot be derived for an existing file. (2) In autonomyGate, have the governed-path comparison run against that canonical repo-relative path rather than against stripSpellings/normalisePath output, so inspectCreate REPORTS the short name as governed at BOTH origins — this is the half that closes the renderer route, and it is the half round 3's fix left to validatePath alone. Keep spellingRefusal and stripSpellings as they are: they are the cheap refusal for names that are not yet synonyms, and the colon strip must stay out of normalise for the measured meta-blob reason already documented. (3) In scripts/verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs §13, add a row per governed path via its short basename, looked up AT RUNTIME (cmd /c dir /x, or `for %I in (path) do @echo %~sI`) rather than hardcoded, because ~1 versus ~2 depends on directory creation order — and skip the row with a printed residual, never a silent pass, on a volume where 8.3 generation is disabled. Assert for each that inspectCreate refuses at BOTH origins, that applyWith refuses, and that the governed file is BYTE-IDENTICAL afterwards. Add one row for the protected loyaltyGuard.cjs via its short name so the step-2 covenant claim is held too.

findings.where: electron/lib/upgradeApplier.cjs — the `proposal.meta.autonomy = { ...(proposal.meta.autonomy || {}), attemptedBy, autonomousApply, flagFromOpts, attemptedAt }` merge at entry, above the schema check, the covenant re-run, the governed-path fence and the per-change validations
findings.problem: A caller-supplied meta.autonomy.appliedBy survives onto an entry that is then persisted FAILED — the exact defect the code's own comment says it fixed. Round 2 moved appliedBy/appliedAt to the success path with the stated reason that an entry refused at the door is persisted FAILED by proposals.cjs and must not carry a field claiming master applied it. The merge spreads the caller's own meta.autonomy and then overwrites only four keys (attemptedBy, autonomousApply, flagFromOpts, attemptedAt); appliedBy and appliedAt are not among them. Measured: an entry whose meta.autonomy was pre-seeded with {appliedBy:'master', appliedAt:'2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', autonomousApply:true, note:'forged'} and refused at step 4 (action 'delete') persisted as {appliedBy:'master', appliedAt:'2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', autonomousApply:false, note:'forged', attemptedBy:'master', flagFromOpts:false, attemptedAt:'…'} — appliedBy survived; same result for a refusal at step 3, the governed-path fence. autonomousApply IS correctly forced to false, which is the field the forward-compatibility argument rests on, so this is an audit-trail integrity defect and not an authorisation one: no byte was written, I6 held, and masterDriven is still derived. It matters because the audit trail of the one component that writes source is how master reconstructs what happened, and "status FAILED" beside "appliedBy: master" is the same contradiction as a badge reading paused over running work — the defect class this project has now fixed three times elsewhere. Reachability: the create fence refuses this design's kinds from IPC, so the renderer cannot seed it directly; the live routes are an in-process proposals.create() and restore() rehydrating a crafted on-disk entry on an id check alone, both of which are already-disclosed residuals rather than new holes. Neither suite seeds meta.autonomy before an apply, so the existing "no field on the entry claims the apply happened" assertion holds only for an entry whose meta the test itself authored.
findings.fix: Build the record from a whitelist instead of spreading an untrusted object: keep the four derived keys plus any explicitly-recognised prior fields, and drop everything else — or, minimally, delete proposal.meta.autonomy.appliedBy and .appliedAt immediately after the spread, so only the success path below the write loop can set them. Then add a suite row that pre-seeds meta.autonomy with {appliedBy:'master', appliedAt:'…', autonomousApply:true}, forces a refusal (a 'delete' action and a governed path are both cheap), and asserts that neither appliedBy nor appliedAt is present on the persisted entry afterwards while autonomousApply is false — the assertion that would have caught this. The existing row asserting appliedBy is written BELOW the write loop in source should stay; it holds the ordering, not the provenance.

findings.where: RAMA_AGI_MASTER_SPEC.md — SECTION 28 ledger row 152; corrected replacement text already prepared in docs/research/self-upgrade-build.md §6 Block B
findings.problem: Ledger row 152 understates its own build. It records "verifyAutonomyStop.cjs (197) and verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs (320) … 2518 -> 3035 assertions, 0 failures" and "Two build-review rounds". Measured by re-running the chain myself: verifyUpgradeApplier.cjs is 433/0 and npm run verify totals 3148 passed, 0 failed across 28 scripts, which matches commit 4b63dbf's message and not the row. The commit message raises the staleness explicitly rather than hiding it, and parks the corrected one-line row in the build note so the spec edit stays a clean one-line insertion that rebases onto dev — a defensible call. But the project's resume protocol makes SECTION 28 the document a cold session resumes from, and a row whose assertion count is 113 short of the suite it describes is the kind of drift that makes a later session re-derive what was already decided. No invariant is affected and nothing is misstated about the design.
findings.fix: Replace row 152 with the corrected text from docs/research/self-upgrade-build.md §6 Block B as a one-line edit — 197 and 433, 2518 -> 3148, three build-review rounds — and add the next concrete step for the open item so the row resumes cold: the governed-path fence must canonicalise via fs.realpathSync.native rather than by string transform (finding 1), with the §13 short-basename rows that hold it.
